In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah Yusuf

It is Meccan by the consensus of the reciters. In the reports: Allah, exalted is He, sent down what He sent down of the Qur'an, and the Muslims recited it for a period. Then they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would relate to us." So Allah, exalted is He, sent down this surah, in which is: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾. Then they said after that: "If only you would speak to us, O Messenger of Allah," so He sent down ﴿Allah has sent down the best discourse﴾. Then they said: "If only you would remind us, O Messenger of Allah," so Allah, exalted is He, sent down: ﴿Has not the time come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah?﴾ All of these refer them back to the Qur'an.

And from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, he said: Surat Yusuf and Surat Maryam are what the people of Paradise will enjoy (yatafakkahu, "delight in") in Paradise.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the noble one, son of the noble one, son of the noble one, son of the noble one, is Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon them all). Had I remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, and then been called to what he was called to, I would have answered." He meant when the king called him from the prison. The report is sound.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾ means: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing." We have already explained other meanings of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) earlier, so we will not repeat them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ means: these verses which I have sent down to you are those verses whose sending down I promised in the Torah and the Gospel. His saying ﴿al-Mubin﴾ means: its lawful and unlawful are clear (al-bayn). It was also said: al-Bayn means its right guidance and its misguidance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 2:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an⟩. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant is: "Indeed, We have sent down the Qur'an in Arabic." In the Musnad narrations of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Love the Arabs for three reasons: because I am an Arab, the Qur'an is in Arabic, and the speech of the people of Paradise is in Arabic." And His words ﴿so that you may understand⟩ mean: so that you may comprehend.

We recite to you the best of stories (﴿نَحن نقص عَلَيْك أحسن الْقَصَص﴾) — "We relate to you the best of stories." The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: its meaning is: We explain to you the reports of the earlier nations and the past generations in the best explanation; and the qāṣṣ (narrator) is the one who conveys the report in its proper form. It was also said: what is meant by the verse is the story of Yusuf specifically; He called it "the best of stories" to increase its honour. (It was also said:) the most wondrous of stories. It was also said: the most judicious of stories. The first is the well-known view. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAṭāʾ that he said: No grieving person hears Surat Yusuf without finding relief in it. And His saying: ﴿بِمَا أَوْحَينَا إِلَيْك هَذَا الْقُرْآن﴾ means: through Our revelation to you of this Qur'an. And His saying: ﴿وَإِن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين﴾ means: and indeed you were, before it, among those unaware of this story and others.

The Exalted's words: ﴿When Joseph said to his father﴾ mean: Remember when Joseph said to his father: ﴿O my father﴾. It was recited in two ways: "yā abat" and "yā abat," with kasra and with fatha. As for the kasra, the original is "yā abatī," then the yā was dropped and the kasra was sufficient. As for the fatha, the original is "yā abatā," then the alif was dropped and the fatha was sufficient. Al-A'shā said:

(O my father, do not leave us here... for we fear that we shall be destroyed.)

His words: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾. In the narrative it is related that Joseph was twelve years old when he saw this vision. It has been said otherwise, and God knows best. It is narrated that he saw this vision on the Night of Power, a Friday night. His words ﴿eleven stars﴾ mean: eleven stars from the stars of the sky, and what was intended by them were his brothers, who were eleven men, by whom one is guided just as one is guided by the stars. His words ﴿and the sun and the moon﴾: the interpretation of the sun is his father, and the interpretation of the moon is his mother. Thus said Qatadah and others. Some said: his mother had died, and this one was his maternal aunt, Rachel. Ibn Jurayj said: the moon is his father and the sun is his mother, because the sun is feminine and the moon is masculine. His words: ﴿I saw them prostrating to me﴾. Some said: "prostrating before me to God." The more correct view is that they prostrated to him as a greeting and an honour. If someone says: "He said ﴿prostrating﴾ (sājidīn, masculine plural) and did not say sājidāt (feminine plural), while the rule of Arabic for stars is to say sājidāt," the answer is: when God the Exalted informed about them using an action of rational beings, which is prostration, He joined them with rational beings in the grammatical construction of the speech, so He said sājidīn, and did not say sājidāt.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 5:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: Indeed, the visions of the prophets are revelation. Ya'qub knew that if the brothers heard this vision, they would recognize that it is true and would envy him. Therefore he commanded him to conceal it for this reason. And His saying: ﴿lest they plot against you a plot﴾ means: lest they devise a stratagem against you. ﴿Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy﴾ means: indeed, Satan adorns that for them and drives them to it because of his enmity, the ancient enmity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And thus will your Lord choose you﴾, means: just as He raised your rank and showed you this vision, so likewise your Lord will choose you, i.e., will select you (yaṣṭafīka rabbuka). ﴿And teach you the interpretation of events﴾: the interpretation (ta'wīl) of [what its outcome will ultimately be]. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by this is the knowledge of interpretation (ta'bīr, the interpreting of dreams) and what dreams will lead to. They said: Yusuf was the most knowledgeable of people in dream-interpretation and the most skilled among them in explaining it.

His saying: ﴿And complete His favour upon you﴾ means: He will make you a prophet, and that is the completion of favour upon the prophets. ﴿And upon the family of Ya'qub﴾, meaning upon the sons of Ya'qub, for all the sons of Ya'qub were prophets. His saying: ﴿As He completed it upon your forefathers before, Ibrahim and Ishaq﴾ means: just as He made the two of them prophets before, so likewise He will make you a prophet.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: its meaning is clear.

It has also been said: what is meant by the completion of favour upon Ibrahim is his deliverance from the fire, and what is meant by the completion of favour upon Ishaq is his deliverance from the slaughter. This is a well-known view. Al-Hasan al-Basri mentioned that there were eighty years between this vision and this statement and its fulfilment. And Abdullah ibn Shaddad mentioned that there were forty years between them. And this is the more well-known of the two views.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 7:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who ask.﴾ In some codices it reads: "a lesson (ibrah) for those who ask." The word "ayat" (signs) is the plural of "ayah," and an ayah (sign) is an indication of a great matter. There are two opinions regarding the meaning of "ayah" here:

The first: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah about the story of Joseph, peace be upon him, and in some narrations they asked him about the cause of the migration of Jacob's sons from Canaan to Egypt. So he related to them the story of Joseph, and they found it to agree with what is in the Torah. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿signs for those who ask﴾, that is, a proof of the prophethood of the Messenger.

The second opinion: The meaning of His words ﴿signs for those who ask﴾ is that they are lessons for those who take heed. They include the mention of the envy of Joseph's brothers toward him and what their affair came to through envy; they include the mention of his dream and what Allah fulfilled of it; they include the patience of Joseph in resisting the desire of sexual gratification, and his servitude in prison, and what his affair came to of kingship; they also include the mention of Jacob's grief and what his affair came to of attaining his desire and the departure of his sorrow, and other things mentioned in the surah. These, then, are lessons for those who take heed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 8:

His saying: ﴿When they said: Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are⦆ — the verse. Joseph and his brother Benjamin were from one mother, and Ya'qub had an intense love for Joseph. Joseph's brothers saw from him an inclination toward Joseph that he did not show toward them, so they uttered this statement. And His saying: ﴿And we are a band⦆ — al-Farra' said: the ʿusbah (band, company) is ten or more. (Al-Qutaybi said:) And from ten up to forty. Others besides them said: "And we are a band" means a group whose members support one another. And His saying: ﴿Indeed our father is in clear error⦆ — its meaning: indeed our father is in obvious mistake. If someone says: How did they describe a messenger of God's messengers, such as Ya'qub, as being in error?

The answer to this: the meaning of "error" (ḍalāl) here is not error in religion; had they intended that, they would have become disbelievers. Rather, what is meant by error here is mistake in managing the affairs of this world, and by this they meant: we are more deserving of love in managing the affairs of this world, because we are more beneficial to him and older than Joseph, and we look after his livelihood for him and tend his livestock for him; so he is mistaken in this respect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Kill Joseph﴾. Qatl (killing): the destruction of the body in such a manner that life cannot remain in it.

And His saying: ﴿or cast him out to some land﴾, meaning: cast him into a land where beasts of prey will devour him. It was also said: cast him to a land far from his father, and far from which his father would be. And His saying: ﴿so that the face of your father may be clear for you﴾, meaning: so that the face of your father may be free for you (i.e., his attention and love will be wholly yours). And His saying: ﴿and after that you may be a righteous people﴾, meaning: repent after you have done this, and persist in righteousness, and God will pardon you.

The People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) have taken this verse as evidence that the repentance of one who has committed intentional murder is accepted, for God, exalted is He, mentioned their resolve to kill and mentioned repentance, and He did not rebuke them for repenting after the killing; this indicates that it is accepted.

Ibn Ishaq said, meaning Muhammad ibn Ishaq: Their deed included several crimes: severing the ties of kinship, disobedience to a parent (father), little compassion toward the small, abandoned child who had done no wrong, betrayal of trust, neglect of the covenant of protection, and the lie they resolved upon together with their father Ya'qub, peace be upon him. Then God pardoned them despite all of this, so that no one would despair of His mercy. Some scholars said: They resolved to kill him, but God, out of compassion and mercy toward them, restrained them from killing him; and had they proceeded to kill him, they would all have perished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 10:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿A speaker among them said﴾. Most scholars hold that this was Yahudha (Judah), and he was the eldest of them. ﴿A speaker among them said: "Do not kill Yusuf, but cast him into the depths of the well, and some passing caravan will pick him up, if you are going to act."﴾

(He was the eldest) in judgment, not in years. This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He was the maternal cousin of Yusuf."

Qatada said: "He was Ruബeel (Reuben)."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: "He was Shim'un (Simeon)." The most correct of these opinions is the first.

As for His words ﴿Do not kill Yusuf﴾, he advised them not to commit this great sin. As for His words ﴿and cast him into the depths of the well﴾, meaning: the bottom of the well. The *ghayaba* (depths) is every place that hides a thing from you and conceals it. The poet said:

(My sons, when my hidden place conceals me, then travel in my stead among the tribe and the family.)

By *ghayaba* is meant the grave, because it hides the dead person and covers him. The *jubb* (well) is the well that has not been lined with stone, because it was simply cut out and had not yet been lined; *jubb* means "a cutting."

As for His words ﴿some passing caravan will pick him up﴾, meaning: some of the travellers will find him. *Iltiqat* (picking up) is taking a thing from where one does not expect it, and *sayyara* (caravan) are the travellers. As for His words ﴿if you are going to act﴾, meaning: if you are resolved to do what you intend.

The scholars differed as to whether they were adults or not when they resolved on this and carried it out.

Most hold that they were grown men, but that they were not yet prophets. The evidence for this is that they said: "and become righteous people after him," and this is only fitting after reaching maturity. It is also shown by their saying: "O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins, for we were sinners," and a child has no sin; this indicates that they were men.

Some said: they were young. This view is not accepted. Those who held this view argued from their saying: "Send him with us tomorrow, he will frolic and play," and play is the act of children, not of grown men.

They replied to this: they did not mention forbidden play, but meant permissible play.

It is related from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he was asked about His words ﴿he will play﴾, and it was said to him: "How could they say 'he will play' when they were prophets?" He said: "This was before God Most High had informed them of their prophethood."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "O our father, what is the matter with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph?"﴾ They first began with a denunciation of him for not sending Joseph with them and for keeping him with himself, away from them, as if they were saying to him: "You do not send him with us, yet you fear us for him?!"

His saying: ﴿And indeed we are sincere advisers to him.﴾ Nusḥ (sincere counsel) here means attending to his welfare. It was also said that it means kindness and tenderness, and its meaning is: we are tender toward him, kind to him, and attentive to his welfare.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 12:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow to enjoy and play, and indeed we will be his guardians.﴾ His saying: ﴿nartaʿ (to enjoy and frolic)﴾. Al-rataʿ (ar-ratʿ, enjoying freely): it is the expansion in pleasures, seeking their various forms to the right and to the left. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: we eat, drink, become active and amuse ourselves. It was recited as "yartaʿ wa-yalʿab" with the yāʾ (third person), and it has the same meaning as the first, except that it refers specifically to Yusuf. It was also recited as "yartaʿī," which is of the form yaftaʿil (yartaʿī) from al-raʿy (pasturing), and its meaning is: he grazes the livestock just as we graze. And His saying: ﴿And indeed we will be his guardians.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: "Truly, it grieves me that you should take him away"﴾. Its meaning: "Truly, it distresses me that you should take him away." Here, grief (al-hazn) is the pain of the heart at separation from the beloved.

As for His saying, ﴿and I fear that the wolf may devour him﴾, in the story: Ya'qub, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had seen in a dream as if a wolf had attacked Yusuf, and he feared this; so he spoke out of that fear. Some of them have said that he meant by "the wolf" them (his sons). This is not correct, because if he had feared them for him, he would not have handed him over to them, and it would not have been permissible for him to do so. Moreover, it is a forced and strained meaning, so it is not permissible to turn to it.

As for His saying, ﴿while you are heedless of him﴾, that is: "heedless" (sahun).

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said: If the wolf devours him while we are a band﴾ means: a group, whose members strengthen one another. And His saying: ﴿Then indeed we would be losers﴾ means: then indeed we would be incapable."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 15:

Allah's statement: ﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him into the depths of the well﴾. Al-ijma' (resolve, determination) is: a firm intention to do something. The waw here is superfluous (muqhamah), and the meaning is: "When they took him away, they resolved to put him into the depths of the well." The poet said:

(They resolved their matter at night, but when they ... awoke, they awoke to find me a thief.)

And His statement ﴿and they agreed [wa-ajma'u] to put him into the depths of the well﴾ means: that they would throw him into the depths of the well. Wahb ibn Munabbih and others mentioned that when they took Yusuf, they treated him with the utmost honour and carried him along until they went out into the open country with him. When they had gone out with him, they threw him down and began to beat him while he cried out for help, until they nearly killed him. Then Yahudha (Judah) prevented them from him. It is also reported that he was between [twelve] years old. This is the well-known account.

In some reports, he was six years old. In some reports, he was seventeen years old. This too is well known.

Then they agreed (to) throw him into the well. They came to a well off the road, wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, and they threw him into it. It is narrated that he clung to the sides of the well, so they tied his hands and then threw him. In some reports, they placed him in a bucket and lowered him into the well, and when he reached the water, there was a rock, and he stood upon it. It is also narrated that they told him: "Sit in that recess of the well, and when someone comes to draw water, catch hold of the bucket until you are pulled out."

Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi said: When Yusuf was in the well, he called upon Allah, saying: "O You who are a witness not absent, O You who overcome without being overcome, O You who are near and not distant, make for me, from what I am in, a relief and a way out."

Then the reports differ as to how many nights he spent in the well. The majority say he spent three nights in it. The other view is that he spent one night in it.

Allah's statement: ﴿And We revealed to him: you will surely inform them of this affair of theirs﴾. The majority of the people of tafsir hold that this revelation was to Yusuf, and that Allah sent Jibril to comfort him and give him good news of his release, and to inform him that he would tell them of what they had done and requite them for it, while they did not recognise that he was Yusuf; and this will come after this story. It was also said: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ means that He revealed to him.

There is another view regarding the verse: that the revelation here is inspiration (ilham); this is like Allah's statement: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa: suckle him﴾. As for Jibril's coming, it was after this.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they came to their father in the evening, weeping﴾. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: They came during the darkness of the evening so that they would be bolder in making their excuse with a lie. It is related that Ya'qub heard their cries and wailing, so he came out and said: "What is wrong with you? Has the wolf harmed any of your sheep?" They said: "No; rather, the wolf has eaten Yusuf."

Al-Hasan recited: "ghashaa'an yabkuna" (﴿غشاء يبكون﴾), and its meaning is: their sight had been clouded by weeping.

"They said, 'O our father, we went off racing one another, and we left Joseph by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him. But you will not believe us, even if we were truthful.'" (Qur'an 12:17)

This means: (we went off) competing (nantadil) and seeing who would win the race (al-sabq). It is also said: we raced on our feet.

It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) raced with ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) twice. In the first race she outran him, and in the second race he outran her, and he said to her: "This is for that."

As for His words, ﴿and we left Joseph by our belongings﴾, meaning: by our clothes and our cloth goods. ﴿So the wolf devoured him, and you will not believe us﴾, meaning: you will not regard us as truthful. ﴿Even if we were truthful﴾, meaning: even if we were truthful.

If someone says: How is it permissible for them to say to the Prophet of Allah: "You do not believe the truthful"?

The answer: its meaning is that if we were truthful in your sight, you would suspect us in this matter because of your intense love for him and your inclination towards him. So how much more so, when you feared for him at the beginning and suspected us regarding his right?

There is also another meaning: that the meaning of His words ﴿and you will not believe us﴾ is that you will not accept what we say, because we have no proof of our truthfulness, even if we are truthful in the sight of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they came upon his shirt with false blood﴾. This is evidence that they removed his shirt from him when they threw him into the well. It is related that he said to them: "Leave me my shirt so that I may cover myself with it." They said to him: "Call upon the sun, the moon and the stars to cover you," meaning: [by] what he had seen of the dream.

His saying: ﴿with false blood﴾. It was said: "with blood," meaning: "with blood possessing falsehood" (dhi kadhib). It was also said: "blood about which lies were told" (makdhub fihi). It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he recited "bi-dam kadhib" with the unmarked dal (kadib), and this is blood that has changed (al-dam al-mutaghayyir).

In the narrative: they smeared the shirt with blood and did not tear it. Ya'qub, upon him be the blessings of God, said: "How did the wolf eat him and not tear his shirt? I have never known the wolf to be gentle." This is related from al-Hasan al-Basri.

And it is related that some of them said: "The thieves killed him." They disagreed about Ya'qub, so he accused them of it, and ﴿he said: Nay, your souls have beautified a matter for you﴾, meaning: you have lied; rather your souls have made an affair seem fair to you. ﴿Amr﴾ (affair). Al-taswil (beautification) means tazyin (making fair). His saying: ﴿So patience is becoming﴾ means: my affair is patience that is becoming. It was also said: "So patience is becoming, which I choose." Al-sabr al-jamil (becoming patience) is that in which there is no complaint and no impatience. His saying: ﴿And God is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ means: God is the One whose help is sought for patience against what you lie about.

In the narrative: they went away and came back with a wolf and said: "This is the one that ate your son." Ya'qub said to it: "O wolf! Did you eat my son and the fruit of my heart?" God, exalted, made it speak and it said: "By God, I never saw your son's face." He said: "Then how did you come to be in the land of Canaan?" It said: "I came for kinship ties." Al-Naqqash related it in his tafsir, and God knows best.

They differed concerning the place of the well into which Yusuf was lowered. Qatada said: it is a well in Bayt al-Maqdis. It was also said: it is a well in the land of al-Urdunn. Muqatil said: it is a well well-known, which was three farsakh between it and the dwelling of Ya'qub, and God knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket.﴾ "Sayyara" (caravan): they are the people traveling, and they were called sayyara because they travel (yasirun) through the earth. And His saying: ﴿they sent their water-drawer﴾, "al-warid" (water-drawer) is the one who goes ahead of the people to draw water from the well. Al-Asma'i said: The Arabs say, "adlaytu al-dalw" (I let down the bucket) when I send it into the well, and "dallaytuha" (I drew it up) when I pull it out of the well.

And His saying: ﴿He said, "O my good news! This is a boy."﴾ In this there are two opinions. The first, and it is the more evident of the two: the meaning of His saying "O my good news!" is, "Rejoice, this is a boy." Reported by al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj.

The second opinion: he called out to his companion, whose name was Bushra, and said, "O Bushra! This is a boy," meaning, "O so-and-so, this is a boy." Reported by al-A'mash and al-Suddi.

In the story: the well was off the road, but the people lost their way until they came upon it. When the water-drawer came and sent down the bucket to seek water, Yusuf clung to it, and they pulled up, thinking it was water. Ibn Mujahid reported from his father that the walls of the well wept for Yusuf until he was brought out of it. Also in the story: the owner of the caravan was Malik ibn Du'ar, a man from Khuza'a. And His saying: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ means: the water-drawer and those with him concealed him as merchandise from the rest of the company, for fear that they would demand a share in him.

And His saying: ﴿as merchandise (bidaa'a)﴾ means: they said, "We will tell the people that the owners of the water have entrusted us with this boy for sale (istab'da'una)." Al-bida'a is a portion of wealth, and al-bad' is a piece. From this is his saying concerning Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her: "She is a part (bad'a) of me," meaning a piece of me. And this is a established report.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what they do﴾ is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 20:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted out﴾. Most of the people of tafsir hold that those who sold him were his brothers, and this is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of the early scholars. The word "shara" (شروه) here means: sold.

The poet said:

(And I sold a cloak, would that I had... after the cloak I would have been an owl)

In the narration: when the people brought Yusuf out of the well, his brothers came and said: "This is a slave who ran away from us," and they threatened Yusuf until he did not know (his condition), and he affirmed what they had said. Then they sold him to them.

The second opinion regarding the verse: that those who sold Yusuf were those who drew him out of the well. The correct view is the first.

And His words: ﴿for a paltry price﴾. Bakhs (بخس), in the language, is deficiency, and the meaning of bakhs here is: unlawful; the unlawful was called bakhs because it is deprived of blessing. This is the saying of al-Sha'bi and others. Some of them said: ﴿for a paltry price﴾ means: possessing injustice. It is related from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas that they both said: a paltry price: counterfeit coins. It was also said: a paltry price, meaning: a little.

They differed over how much the price was. Mujahid said: it was [twenty-two] dirhams, and the brothers were eleven men, so they divided it, and each one took two dirhams, except Yahudha, for he took nothing. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: they sold him for twenty dirhams. It was also said: [they sold him] for forty.

His words ﴿a few dirhams counted out﴾ mean: they counted them by counting and did not weigh them by weight, because of their small number. He said: they did not weigh anything less than an ounce, which is forty dirhams.

His words ﴿And they were of those who showed little interest in him﴾ mean: they had no desire for Yusuf, because they did not recognise his honour with Allah. It was also said: they were of those who showed little interest in the price, in the sense that their aim was not the price; rather, their aim was to remove Yusuf far from his father.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 21:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son."﴾ In the Stories (al-Qasas) it is related that Malik ibn Du'ar brought him to Egypt and offered him for sale, and Qitfir, the chief officer and treasurer of the king, bought him. It is also said that his name was Qintur. He was called al-Aziz, and no one in Egypt was called by his name, out of honor and dignity. It is narrated that he bought him for twenty dinars, a pair of sandals, and a garment. Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned that when he was offered for sale, the people bid against one another for his price, until his price reached his weight in gold, his weight in silver, his weight in musk, and his weight in silk; his weight was four hundred and two hundred ratl (...). Wahb said: He was thirteen years old at that time. We have already explained that according to the view of some of them, he was seventeen years old. Ka'b and others said: He was among the most beautiful of people in face, having the form of Adam when He created him. ﴿Perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son; and thus We established Joseph in the land, and that We might teach him the interpretation of events﴾ from God, the Exalted, before he committed the sin. In some reports it is said: "Joseph was given half of beauty." This is strange. It is also said that he was transferred to his grandmother Sarah, and Sarah had been given a sixth of beauty.

As for His saying, ﴿his wife﴾, it is said that her name was Raghil. It is also said that her name was Zulaykha.

As for His saying, ﴿Make his residence comfortable﴾, its meaning is: honor him in food, clothing, and lodging. Al-mathwa (residence) in the language means the place of dwelling, and it is said: thawa bi-l-makan when he stayed in the place.

As for His saying, ﴿perhaps he will benefit us﴾, it means: we will sell him for profit if we wish to sell, or he will benefit us through service if we do not sell him. As for His saying, ﴿or we may adopt him as a son﴾, it means: or we will free him and adopt him. It has been established from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, by the narration of Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from him, that he said: The most perceptive of people are three: the Aziz regarding Joseph when he said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable; perhaps he will benefit us"; the daughter of Shu'ayb regarding Moses, peace be upon him, when she said, "O father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one"; and Abu Bakr regarding Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he appointed him as his successor.

As for His saying, ﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land﴾, its meaning is: just as We rescued him from destruction and saved him from the darkness of the well, so We established him in the land. The land here is the land of Egypt. As for His saying, ﴿established him﴾, it means (by granting him authority), extending his hand, and raising his station until he reached what he reached.

As for His saying, ﴿and that We might teach him the interpretation of events﴾, this has been explained before. As for His saying, ﴿And Allah is dominant over His affair﴾, there are two opinions regarding it. The first: Allah is dominant over His affair; no preventer prevents Him from it, and no one who wills turns Him back from what He wills.

The second opinion: Allah is dominant over the affair of Joseph through management and protection until He brings him to the end of His knowledge concerning him. As for His saying, ﴿but most people do not know﴾, it is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when he reached his full strength﴾. Most scholars hold that al-ashudd (full strength) is thirty-three years, and it is at this point that it ends, meaning the vigour of youth. It is also said: thirty years. It is also said: from the completion of [eighteen] years up to forty. Mālik was asked about al-ashudd and said: it is maturity of judgement (al-ḥulm).

His saying ﴿We gave him judgement and knowledge﴾ means: understanding (fiqh) and reason. It is also said: judgement (ḥukm) is prophethood, and knowledge (ʿilm) is understanding (fiqh) of the religion. The difference between the ḥakīm (one endowed with wisdom) and the ʿālim (scholar) is that the scholar is one who knows things, while the ḥakīm is one who acts according to what knowledge requires. It is also said: he is one who restrains himself from what he is ignorant of and what is foolish, and from this comes the term ḥikmah (bridle) for the animal, because it restrains the animal from corruption. The poet said:

(O Banū Ḥanīfah, restrain your foolish ones ... indeed I fear for you that I may become angry.)

Meaning: restrain your foolish ones.

His saying: ﴿And thus We reward the good-doers﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 23:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him from himself﴾. The meaning of al-murawadah (seeking to seduce) is seeking the act, and what is meant here is that she invited him to immorality (fahisha). His words: ﴿And she closed the doors﴾ means she shut the doors and made them secure. It is said that she closed seven doors. His words: ﴿And she said, "Come, [I am] yours"﴾ mean: hallum (come here). This is the view of most of the exegetes. It has also been said that it means: come, I am yours. It was recited as "hayta laka" (hayta laka), meaning: I have prepared myself for you (tahayya'at laka). Al-Kisa'i rejected this recitation. The poet said regarding the word "hayta":

(Convey to the Commander of the Faithful ... a brother of Iraq, when we come to him)

(That Iraq and its people ... are bowing their necks toward you, so come, come.)

His words: ﴿He said, "I seek refuge in Allah"﴾ mean: he said, "I take refuge in Allah," that is, I hold fast to Him, "Indeed, He is my Lord."

Most of them said that he meant by this the Aziz; its meaning is: indeed, he is my master (sayyidi). His words: ﴿Indeed, He is my Lord; he has made my residence good﴾ mean: he has honored my residence. His words: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ mean: indeed, adulterers and sinners will not be made happy.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 24:**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾ [the verse]. *Al-hamm* (intention, inclination) is approaching an act without entering into it. As for His words, ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾, her *hamm* was her resolve to commit disobedience and fornication. As for the *hamm* of Yusuf, know that it has been reliably transmitted from Abdullah ibn Abbas that he was asked about His words ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ and said: "He sat with her as the circumciser sits, and he loosened his *himyan* (belt-pouch)." This was narrated by Ibn Abi Mulaykah, Ata', and others. And from Mujahid, who said: "He untied his trousers and began to work at his garments." This is the view of most of the earlier scholars, among them Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Dahhak, and others.

Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said: "Some people have denied this view, but the correct view is what the earliest scholars of this community said, for they were too knowledgeable about Allah to speak about the prophets without knowledge." Ibn al-Anbari also said likewise. Some later scholars claimed that the *hamm* of her (*kana minha*) was her resolve to commit disobedience, while the *hamm* of him was a passing thought in the heart and a strong love accompanied by desire.

In the narrative: the woman said to him, "How beautiful are your eyes!" He said, "They are the first thing that will flow from my face in my grave." She said, "How beautiful is your hair!" He said, "It is the first thing that will be spread out in my grave." She said, "Indeed, the silk bedding is spread out, so get up and fulfill my need." He said, "Then my share of Paradise will be lost." She said, "Indeed, the garden is thirsty, so get up and water it." He said, "Indeed, the key is in the hand of another." He said: Then Satan came and entered between them, and began to tempt him and tempted her, until she desired him and he desired her. Then Allah, the Exalted, rescued His servant and His prophet by the proof that He mentioned.

Qatrib said: the meaning of His words ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ is: "And he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord."

All the other grammarians rejected this view and said: "The Arabs do not place *lawla* (had it not been for) after the verb; rather, the Arabic usage is only to place it first. They say, 'Had it not been for such-and-such, I would have done such-and-such,' and they do not say, 'I did such-and-such had it not been for such-and-such.'" Some of them said: "*Wa-hamma bihā*" means: he intended to strike her and push her away from himself. But this is a distant interpretation. Some of the exegetes said: it is possible that the degree of *hamm* that Yusuf experienced was, in that law, among the minor sins that may be attributed to the prophets. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah, the Exalted, did not mention the sins of the prophets in the Qur'an in order to reproach them with them; rather, He mentioned them to show the favor of pardon bestowed upon them, and so that no one would despair of His mercy. It was also said: He tested them with sins so that He might single them out for purity and honor, and so that all creation would meet Him on the Day of Resurrection in a state of humility over disobedience.

As for His words ﴿had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord﴾, most of the exegetes said: he saw Ya'qub, peace be upon him, [slapping] him on the chest while saying to him: "Will you do the deed of the foolish while you are in the register of the prophets?"

Layth narrated from Ibn Abbas that [Yusuf] sat before her as a man sits before his wife, and then he saw a palm without wrist or upper arm, on which was written: ﴿And indeed, over you are watchers, noble and recording﴾. He was frightened and fled. Then he returned, and that palm appeared again with writing on it: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way﴾. He was frightened and fled. Then he returned and saw that palm once more with writing on it: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾. He was frightened and fled. Then he returned; so Allah said to Jibril: "Overtake My servant before he commits the sin." So he came and wiped him with his wing until his desire came out through his fingertips.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said: the meaning of the *burhan* (proof) is that there was an idol in the house, and the woman got up and covered it with a cloth. Yusuf said to her: "Why did you do this?" She said: "I was ashamed before it to see me while I was committing the disobedience." Yusuf said: "I have more right to be ashamed before my Lord," and he fled.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the *burhan* is that Allah, the Exalted, put into the heart of Yusuf the sanctity of fornication and the severity of its punishment, so he fled and left. Al-Naqqash related that when he drew near to her, he saw a white hair in her nose, so he disliked her and left her. This is a distant view; the most correct of these views is the first.

It has been related that when Ya'qub, peace be upon him, appeared to him, he slapped him on the chest and said: "O Yusuf, before you commit fornication you are like a bird in the air [and cannot be caught], but when you commit fornication you become like a bird that falls and dies. Before you commit fornication you are like an ox that cannot be controlled, but when you commit fornication you become like an ox that perishes, and ants enter into the roots of its horn."

As for His words ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality﴾: *al-su'* (evil) is the ugly praise (i.e., ill repute), and *al-fahsha'* (immorality) is the act of fornication. If it is said: this is evidence that he did not intend fornication and did not aim at it, we say: No; this refers to after the *hamm*. If it is said: did he not say in the course of the surah: ﴿That he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾? We say: It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when Yusuf said this, Jibril said to him: "Nor when you desired?" He said: "I do not absolve myself; indeed, the soul is a commander to evil."

As for His words ﴿Indeed, he was of Our sincere servants﴾: it has been read as *al-mukhlaṣīn* (with fatha on the lam) and *al-mukhliṣīn* (with kasra on the lam). The meaning of *al-mukhliṣ* (one who makes sincere) is one who sincerely devotes his obedience to Allah, and the meaning of *al-mukhlaṣ* (one who is made sincere) is one whom Allah has purified and chosen.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 25:

The words of the Most High: ﴿[And they both raced] to the door﴾. It is related that Yusuf hastened to the door to open it and go out, while the woman hastened to the door to hold it shut so that Yusuf would not get out. So Yusuf got ahead, and the woman caught up with him and seized his shirt and tore it from behind. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and tore his shirt from behind﴾, that is: she split it. And His words: ﴿and they found her master at the door﴾ mean: they found the woman's husband at the door, and the woman hastened ahead, ﴿saying, "What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your wife, except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"﴾. Then she feared for him that he might be killed, so she said: ﴿except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment﴾, meaning he be beaten with whips. When Yusuf heard her words

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verses 26–27:

﴿He said: "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself."﴾ That is: she asked me for indecency (al-fahisha).

As for His words, ﴿And a witness from her own family testified﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first is that the witness was an infant in the cradle. He who held this view said: this is the opinion of Abu Hurayra, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak, and it is one of the two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Hurayra said: "Three infants spoke in the cradle: 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, the companion of Juraij, and the witness of Yusuf."

The second opinion is that the witness was a wise man from the woman's relatives, who was standing with her husband. He heard the commotion from behind the door and saw the tear in the shirt, and so he said the statement, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verses 26–27:

﴿He said: "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself."﴾ That is: she asked me for indecency (al-fahisha).

As for His words, ﴿And a witness from her own family testified﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first is that the witness was an infant in the cradle. He who held this view said: this is the opinion of Abu Hurayra, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak, and it is one of the two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Hurayra said: "Three infants spoke in the cradle: 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, the companion of Juraij, and the witness of Yusuf."

The second opinion is that the witness was a wise man from the woman's relatives, who was standing with her husband. He heard the commotion from behind the door and saw the tear in the shirt, and so he said the statement, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.﴾ and the rest of the verse.

And His saying: ﴿When he saw that his shirt was torn from behind﴾, he knew that the fault was hers. ﴿He said: "Indeed, it is of your guile (kayd). Indeed, your guile is great."﴾ And in the narrative: he was lacking in protective jealousy (hamiyya) and zeal (ghayra). Then he said to Yusuf:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 29:

﴿Yusuf, turn away from this﴾. That is: do not mention this, so that it does not spread. Then he said to the woman: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, that is, repent to God Most High, ﴿for you were among the sinners﴾. The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 30:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And women in the city said, "The wife of the chief official is seeking to seduce her servant boy from himself."﴾ "The city" here means the city of Egypt. It has also been said that it is the city of Ayn Shams.

As for "the women," they said: They were five women: the wife of the king's chamberlain, the wife of the master of the beasts, the wife of the master of the food, the wife of the master of the drink, and the wife of the master of the prison. Some of them said: They were women from among the noblewomen of Egypt.

His words: ﴿the wife of the chief official﴾. It has been said that "al-'Aziz" is the one who is mighty by his power, protected against being wronged in his affairs. His words: ﴿is seeking to seduce her servant boy from himself﴾. Fata (servant boy) here means: her slave. The meaning is that she was asking her slave [to] commit the sin of fornication. His words ﴿She has certainly captivated him with love﴾: it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with her, that he said: "Shaghafaha hubban" means: overcame her. It is also narrated from him that he said: "Shaghafaha hubban" means: love entered into the shaghaf of her heart, and shaghaf of the heart is its inner part. It has also been said: shaghaf of the heart is the membrane of the heart, as if love tore through the membrane, reached the heart and overpowered it. It has also been said: shaghaf of the heart is the core (suwaydaa') of the heart. It has also been said: the kernel (habbat) of the heart. A poet said:

(And there is no passion except a lesser passion that you have felt... it struck the shaghaf of the heart, so the heart is captivated.)

In the irregular reading, it was recited "sha'afaha" hubban, and its meaning: love carried her in every direction, and from it comes sha'af al-jibal, meaning its peaks.

His words: ﴿Indeed, we see her in manifest error﴾, meaning: in clear mistake. It is also said: "in manifest error" means: that she has abandoned what such women are accustomed to, of modesty and chastity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 31:

His saying: ﴿When she heard of their scheming﴾ means: of their plotting. It is narrated that she had confided her secret to them and made them swear to keep it, but they divulged it; for this reason he called it a scheme (makr). His saying: ﴿and she sent for them﴾ means: she invited them. His saying: ﴿and prepared for them a reclining banquet (muttaka)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: the muttaka is that on which they recline on cushions. It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "As for me, I do not eat reclining." This is among the humility that Allah chose for him. As for tyrants and the great, they have become accustomed to eating while reclining. It has also been said: ﴿and prepared for them a reclining banquet﴾ means: food, drink and reclining.

In the irregular reading (shadhdh) it is recited: "and prepared for them a muttak." The muttak is the citron (utrujj). This was reported by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid. It has also been said that it is the bazmaward (a fruit); this was cited by al-Dahhak. It has also been said that it is anything that is cut with a knife. In the story: she invited forty women from the noblewomen of Egypt, and she adorned a house with various fruits, cushions, and spread out carpets. His saying: ﴿and gave each one of them a knife﴾ means: she gave each one of them a knife, for they used to eat meat by cutting it with a knife; and the sunnah is to tear (nahsh).

His saying: ﴿and she said: "Come out before them"﴾: she ordered Joseph to come out before them, so he came out, and they had taken up knives to cut what they were eating. His saying: ﴿So when they saw him, they were struck with awe of him (akbarnahu)﴾: there are two opinions regarding it. The first: they magnified him. The second: they menstruated. The poet said:

(We approach women in their pure states, and we do not approach women when they are akbarna ikbaran)

meaning: when they menstruate. The first is the more appropriate. Abu 'Ubayda rejected that "akbarna" could mean "menstruated."

His saying: ﴿and cut their hands﴾: most of the scholars hold that this was scratching and wounding without severing. Some said that they cut their hands completely. The first is more correct. It is said: "Fulan cut his hand" when he scratched and wounded it.

In the story: they were dumbfounded, their minds departed, and they cut their hands without knowing it, until blood flowed from them. His saying: ﴿and they said: "Allah forbid!"﴾ It is also read: "hasha lillah," and its meaning: [God forbid] that this should be ﴿a human being; this is not human﴾, meaning: a human like the rest of mankind. It is read: "ma hadha mushtariyan," meaning: a purchased slave. His saying: ﴿This is none but a noble angel (malak karim)﴾ means: a noble angel in the sight of his Lord. It is narrated by Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Joseph was given half of beauty." Ibn Ishaq, the author of al-Ma'ani, said: Joseph and his mother took two-thirds of beauty.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the story of the Mi'raj, that "he saw Joseph in the third heaven, and he said: 'I saw his face like the full moon.'" It is also related that when he walked through the streets of Egypt, a light was seen reflected from his face on the walls. It is also related that when he became king, whenever a woman entered upon him, he would cover his face so that she would not be tempted by him.

He said: "Then that is the one you blamed me for." Al-Malama (blame) is describing someone with something ugly in a belittling way. The meaning of her words "Then that is the one you blamed me for" is: this is the one you blamed me for. Then she openly stated what she had done, and said: ﴿And I did seek to seduce him, but he refused.﴾ She stated it openly because she knew that after that there would be no blame upon her from them, since they had been afflicted by what afflicted them from seeing him.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But he refused⌋ (fa-ista'sama), meaning he abstained. And His saying: ﴿And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned﴾, meaning: he will surely be punished by imprisonment. And His saying: ﴿and he will surely be among the humbled﴾, meaning: he will surely be among those who are despised and abased.

It is narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih that those women fell in love with him, and a group of them died from their love for him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 33:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me."﴾ It is recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "Rabb al-sijn" (the Lord of the prison). Al-habs (confinement) and al-sijn (the prison) mean the place of confinement. ﴿That to which they invite me﴾ It is said: had he not said this, he would not have been tried with prison. In some reports it is said: "Affliction is entrusted to speech," and the better course for a person is to ask Allah for well-being (al-'afiyah).

As for His saying, ﴿that to which they invite me﴾, there are two views concerning it. The first: the invitation came from her alone, but he attributed it to all the women, moving from explicit speech to allusion (al-ta'rid).

The second view: all of them invited him to themselves.

As for His saying, ﴿And unless You turn away their plot from me, I will incline toward them﴾, its meaning is: unless You turn away their evil from me. ﴿I will incline toward them﴾ meaning: I will lean toward them. The poet said:

(How long will you yearn, while your head is grey? Did you think death would mistake you for someone else?)

As for His saying, ﴿and I will be among the ignorant﴾, this is evidence that the believer, if he commits a sin, commits it out of ignorance. It was also said its meaning is: and I will be among the blameworthy, just as a person is blamed for doing something he undertakes while ignorant.

Allah's saying: ﴿So his Lord responded to him﴾, meaning: his Lord answered him. And His saying: ﴿and turned away from him their scheming﴾, meaning: their evil. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ — its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 35:

His saying: ﴿Then it appeared to them﴾ means: it became evident to them. And His saying: ﴿after they had seen the signs﴾ here refers to the tearing of the shirt, the speech of the infant, the women cutting their hands with knives, and their minds being taken away by what they saw of his beauty. And His saying: ﴿that they should imprison him for a time﴾ means: that they should confine him for a period. ʿAṭāʾ said: "for a time" means until the talk of the people ceases.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 36:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men﴾. In the narrative: the woman said to her husband, "This Hebrew youth has disgraced me among the people. Either you permit me to go out and make my excuses to the people, or you imprison him." So he imprisoned him. After that, when he had been imprisoned, the king imprisoned two men from among his close associates: one of them the keeper of his food, and the other the keeper of his drink. It is said that one of them was called Sarhum and the other Shirhum. The reason for their imprisonment was that the king suspected the keeper of the food of intending to poison him, and he also thought that the keeper of the drink had colluded with him in this. The king was al-Walid ibn Marwan al-'Amliqi, and it has been said that the name is other than this.

And His saying: ﴿One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine."﴾ It is narrated that when Yusuf, peace be upon him, entered the prison, he began to call to God and spread his knowledge. He saw these two men, and they were distressed, so he asked them about their condition. They mentioned that they were the king's companions, and that the king had imprisoned them, and that they had seen a dream which had grieved them. So he said to them, "Recount to me what you have seen," and they recounted their dreams to him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine."﴾ And in the narrative: he said, "I saw a vine upon which were three clusters; I plucked them and pressed them into wine, and I gave the king to drink from it."

And His saying: ﴿pressing wine﴾. Al-'Asr (pressing) is leaning on something containing moisture with the hand so that its water is squeezed out. And His saying: ﴿wine (khamran)﴾: it has been said, grapes. It has been said this is in the dialect of Oman. Al-Mu'tamir said: "I met a Bedouin who had a basket with grapes in it, and I said, 'What do you have with you?' He said, 'Khamr (wine).'" And the poet said:

(My boon companion, a true friend, contends with me over it,
the roasted fowl and the grapes of the vine.)

By "grapes" he meant wine. It is also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿pressing wine﴾ is, i.e., grapes that become wine. It is also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿pressing wine﴾ is, i.e., grapes; he named it wine by the name of what it will become. The Arabs say: "So-and-so presses date syrup and bakes bricks," meaning: he presses grapes for syrup, and boils clay for bricks. The poet said:

(Praise be to God, the Majestic, the Bountiful,
the crumbled bread has become on the tops of the sticks.)

And His saying: ﴿And the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread upon my head, of which the birds eat."﴾ It is narrated that the other said: "Indeed, I see myself as if I were carrying three baskets of bread on my head, and birds of prey pecking from it."

And His saying: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers.﴾ He said: When Yusuf, peace be upon him, saw a sick person in the prison, he would visit him and attend to him; when a person was in poverty, he would gather something for him; when he saw someone wronged, he would support him; when he saw someone grieved, he would console him. And despite this, he would stand in prayer the whole night.

The second opinion: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers﴾ means: among the good-doers in interpreting dreams. And ihsan (goodness) here carries the sense of knowledge; it is said: "So-and-so is good at such-and-such" (yuhsinu kadha), meaning: he knows it well.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "No food will come to you as provision but that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you"﴾, and so on. Yusuf, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, began, before interpreting the dream, by displaying a miracle and calling to the tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness) of Allah. So his saying, ﴿No food will come to you as provision but that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you﴾, has three opinions.

The first: "You will not call for food from your dwellings but that I will inform you of its quantity, its color, its taste, and the time at which it reaches you, before it reaches you." This miracle is like the miracle of ʿIsa (peace be upon him), and His saying: ﴿And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses﴾.

The second opinion: it was the custom of the king that when he wanted to kill a person, he would send to him a food known among them, and when he wanted to honor a person, he would send to him a food known among them. This is the meaning of his saying: ﴿No food will come to you as provision﴾.

The third opinion: "No food will come to you as provision in the dream but that I will inform you of its interpretation while awake." They said, "From where do you have this? Are you a soothsayer or an astrologer?" He said, "No; rather, it is from what my Lord has taught me." This is the meaning of his saying: ﴿That is from what my Lord has taught me﴾. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers﴾, it is apparent.

Then he said: ﴿And I follow the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob﴾. He made clear that he is a prophet and that he is from the descendants of the prophets. His saying: ﴿It is not for us to associate anything with Allah﴾ means: Allah has protected us from associating partners with Him. His saying: ﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon the people﴾ means by it: what He established of proof and what He made clear of guidance. His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not give thanks﴾ is clear in meaning.

Then he increased in evidence for tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness) and said:

O my two fellow prisoners! ﴿Are many diverse lords better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?﴾ He called them "my two fellow prisoners" because they were in prison. And His saying ﴿Are many diverse lords...﴾ means: lords (ʾarbāb) who are distinct from one another. This one is of gold, that one of silver, that one of copper, and that one of wood. It was also said: this one is highest, this one is middle, and this one is lowest. And His saying ﴿...better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?﴾: "the One" (al-Wāḥid) is the one who overcomes everything, and the purpose is the complete negation of any goodness in them whatsoever. We have mentioned this before. Then he added and said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 40:

﴿What you worship besides Him﴾, that is, besides Allah, ﴿are only names you and your fathers have named﴾. He means: these idols are mere names, bare and empty of meaning. As for His words, ﴿for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾, that is, no proof. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾, there is no judgment except Allah's. ﴿He has commanded that you worship none but Him﴾, its meaning is clear. As for His words, ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is, the straight path. ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾, its meaning is clear.

In the story: when the lord of the prison heard what he (Yusuf) said and saw what he saw from him, he loved him intensely and placed him in charge of the prisoners. Likewise, the prisoners loved him, so much so that a man would be released from prison and then return to him. It is related that the lord of the prison said to him: "I love you." He said: "I implore you by Allah not to love me," meaning: do not love me, "for whoever loves me brings me into trouble. My aunt loved me and I fell into trouble; my father loved me and I was thrown into the well; the wife of the ruler loved me and I was imprisoned." It is also related that the two companions of the king said this statement to him, and he answered them with this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 41:

His saying: ﴿O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his lord of wine﴾. It is related that he said to the companion of the drink: "As for the interpretation of your vision: you will be summoned after three days and restored to your position with the king."

And His saying: ﴿But as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head﴾. He said: "As for you, O companion of the food, you will be summoned after three days and crucified, and the birds will eat from your head." It is related that both of them said: "We lied; we saw nothing." So he said: ﴿The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire﴾, meaning: the matter is finished, and what I said will occur, whether you saw it or did not see it.

Abu Mijlaz said: The one who said to him, "I did not see anything," was specifically the companion of the food. It has also been related that both of them had indeed seen what they described, in reality.

His saying: ﴿The matter has been decreed﴾ is a completion of the speech (tatmim al-kalam).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 42:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he said to the one of them whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord"﴾ means: he was certain (ayqan) that he would be saved from the two of them. ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ means: to your master. It is narrated that he said to him: "Tell the king that there is in the prison a wronged man whose imprisonment has been prolonged."

And His saying: ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the mention of his lord﴾. Most exegetes say its meaning is: Satan caused Yusuf to forget the mention of his lord, until he sought help from a creature like himself. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and others.

The second view: Satan caused the man who was released from the prison to forget the mention of Yusuf to his master.

And His saying: ﴿So he remained in the prison for several years﴾. Most exegetes hold that "several years" (bid' sinin) here means seven years, and he had already remained five years before that, so he remained in it [twelve] years. Al-Akhfash said: the bid' (a few) is from one to ten. It was also said: from three to nine. It is narrated that God, exalted is He, sent Jibril to him, and said to him: "Say, O Yusuf, who made you beloved to your father?" He said: "You, O Lord." He said: "Who delivered you from the well?" He said: "You, O Lord." He said: "Who turned away from you evil and indecency?" He said: "You, O Lord." He said: "Then were you not ashamed before Me that you sought help from a creature?" ﴿By My might, I will surely prolong your stay in the prison.﴾ It is also narrated that he said: "O Lord, by the right of my fathers, forgive me my sin." Jibril came and said to him: "And what right do your fathers have over Me?" As for your grandfather Ibrahim: I made the fire cool and safe for him. As for Isma'il: I ransomed him with a great ram. As for your father Ya'qub: I gave him twelve sons and took one of them from him, and he kept weeping until his eyes turned white and he complained of Me. Yusuf said: "My God, by Your ancient kindness, Your great favour, and Your many blessings, forgive me my sin," and He forgave him.

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: Jibril entered upon Yusuf, peace be upon them both, in the prison, and said to him: "Yusuf, O brother of those who warn, what are you doing among the sinners?" Jibril said to him: "O good son of good ones, your Lord says to you: Were you not ashamed before Me that you sought help from a creature like yourself? By My might, I will surely prolong your imprisonment." Yusuf, peace be upon him, said to him: "Is He pleased with me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I do not mind."

It is narrated that he said to Jibril: "What did the grief of my father Ya'qub reach?" He said: "The grief of seventy bereaved mothers." He said: "And what is its reward?" He said: "The reward of a hundred martyrs."

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the king said, "Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones"﴾. "The king" here means the king of Egypt, and "the king" is the one who has power and wide authority, whose command extends to matters of governance and management. His words ﴿Indeed, I see﴾ mean: "Indeed, I see in a dream." His words ﴿cows﴾: al-Baqar (cattle) is a well-known animal suitable for ploughing, and from it comes the proverb: "The ploughing is upon the cattle," because it is the most suitable for it.

His words ﴿fat﴾ are clear in meaning.

It is narrated that the king saw seven fat cows coming out of the sea, the fattest that cattle could be, and after them there came out seven lean cows in the extreme of emaciation and leanness. Then the lean ones swallowed the fat ones and devoured them, so that no trace of them could be seen on the lean ones. Then he saw ﴿seven green ears of grain and others dry﴾, that is: seven dry ears of grain that had overtaken the green ones until they prevailed over them, so that nothing of their greenness remained. His words ﴿O chiefs, explain to me my dream, if you are able to interpret dreams﴾: the dream (ru'ya) is what a person imagines in sleep. We have already explained that the Prophet said regarding a true dream: "That is an early good news for the believer." It is also narrated from the Prophet that he said: "When time draws near, the dream of the believer will hardly be false." This has two meanings: First, that the drawing near of time is the equality of night and day, and the temperaments are most sound at the equality of night and day; so the dream is more truthful. The second meaning: that the drawing near of time is the nearness of the Hour. It has also been narrated concerning the beginning of the Prophet's revelation: "that when he saw a dream, it came like the break of dawn."

His words ﴿if you are able to interpret dreams﴾: it is said, "I interpreted the dream" (ʿabartu al-ru'ya) when one explains it, and here ta'bir (interpretation) means tafsir (explanation).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 44:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿They said: "They are confused dreams (adghath ahlam)."﴾ Al-Dghath (ضغث, "bundle" or "handful"): everything that one grasps of mixed things, such as herbage and other things.

The meaning of the verse: It is narrated from Qatadah that he said: adghath ahlam, that is, mixtures of dreams (akhlat ahlam). And from Mujahid, he said: "ahawil ahlam" (frightful or confused dreams). It was also said: "abatil ahlam" (false dreams). And His words, ﴿and we are not versed in the interpretation of dreams﴾ (and its meaning): "and we are not people who know the interpretation of dreams (which are) of this description."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 45:

His saying: ﴿And the one of the two who had been saved said, and he remembered after a period (ummah)﴾. That is: after a period of time (muddah). In the narrative, the king gathered the magicians, the soothsayers and the interpreters and related his dream to them. When they were unable to interpret it, he was greatly distressed. Then the young servant who was the cupbearer remembered the condition of Yusuf, peace be upon him, and he was brought to the matter. He came before the king and said: "In the prison there is a man confined, and he interprets dreams," and he mentioned his story. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And the one of the two who had been saved said, and he remembered after a period (ummah)﴾. Here ummah carries the meaning of "time" (hin). We have already explained that he remained in prison for seven years after he interpreted the dream of the king's companion. It is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: Yusuf remained in prison for seven years, and Ayyub remained in affliction for seven years.

It is recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "wa-dhakara ba'da ummah" with a ha' (ummah-ah), and its meaning is: after forgetfulness (nisyan). His saying: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ means: I will bring you its interpretation. ﴿So send me forth﴾ means: send me, O king, to him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 46:

And His saying: ﴿Yusuf, O man of truth (al-siddiq)﴾ in the verse is an abbreviation (ikhtisar), and its meaning is: that the king sent him (the messenger) to Yusuf, and he said: "Yusuf, O man of truth (al-siddiq)." And al-siddiq is one who abounds in truthfulness (al-kathir lil-sidq).

And His saying: ﴿Give us interpretation (aftina)﴾ means: give us an answer (ajibana), ﴿concerning seven fat cows which seven lean ones devour, and seven green ears [of grain] and others dry﴾. This is the mention of the narration of the man's recounting of the king's dream to Yusuf.

And His saying: ﴿That I may return to the people, that they may know﴾ has two interpretations. The first: "That I may return to the people, that they may know the interpretation of the dream." The second, [its meaning is]: "That I may return to the people, that they may know your station and your rank in knowledge."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: "You will sow for seven years, consistently"﴾. This is a statement in the sense of a command; its meaning is: "Sow for seven years," that is, in your customary manner. And al-Da'b (the custom, habit) is al-'Adah (habit, custom). His saying ﴿so what you reap﴾: al-Hisad (the harvest) is well known. His saying: ﴿leave it in its ear﴾: He commanded them to leave the wheat in the ears (spikes), so that it would be more lasting over time. His saying: ﴿except a little of what you eat﴾: that is, of what you thresh and eat. It is as if He commanded them to store away the greater part and to eat according to the measure of need.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 48:

And His saying: ﴿Then there will come after that seven hard years which will consume what you have stored up for them⁠﴾ — he called the years of drought "hard" (shidad) because of their severity upon the people. And His saying: ﴿which will consume what you have stored up for them⁠﴾ means: they will destroy and ruin what you have stored up for them. This is in the manner of extension and metaphor (tawassu' wa-majaz), for years do not consume anything, rather it is the people who consume during years of drought. And His saying: ﴿except a little of what you guard⁠﴾ means: what you keep safe (tuhrizun); and its meaning is: you keep safe for seed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 49:

And His saying: ﴿Then after that there will come a year in which people will be given rain (yughathu), and in which they will press (yaʿsirun)﴾. Al-ghiyath (relief, abundant rain) here means fertility and abundance. As for His saying ﴿and in which they will press﴾, it has been recited with two readings: "yaʿsirun" and "taʿsirun". Its meaning is: they will press oil from the olives, juice from the grapes, and oil (dihn) from sesame. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid.

It was also said: yaʿsirun means: they will be saved (yanjuna). The poet said:

(And one thirsty, calling for relief, is not relieved... and indeed it was the means of salvation for the one who was saved)

And indeed it was ʿasrat al-manjud, meaning: the place of rescue (al-manjat). It was also said: yaʿsirun means: rain will fall upon them from the clouds. God Most High said: ﴿And We sent down from the pressing clouds water pouring forth﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 50:

The saying of the Exalted, ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me."﴾ There is also an abridgement in the verse, for the man returned to the king and related to him the interpretation of the dream, and then the king said: "Bring him to me." And His saying: ﴿So when the messenger came to him, he said﴾ (Return to your lord) — to your master — ﴿and ask him what was the matter with the women who﴾ — that is, what was the state of the women who ﴿cut their hands﴾ — as we have explained before. He did not explicitly mention the wife of the ʿAzīz, out of courtesy and respect. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot﴾ — that is, Knowing of their deceit and their cunning.

Know that it has been authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Had I remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, and then the summoner had come to me, I would have answered (him)." And in some narrations, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on my brother Yusuf; he was a man of forbearance and patience, and had I been in his place and been summoned, I would have hastened (to respond)."

If it is said: What did Yusuf (peace be upon him) intend by refusing the messenger and mentioning the women, when that long time had passed?

The answer: The purpose was that the king should not look upon him with the eye of suspicion, and that he should come to him after the doubts about his case had been removed. Therefore he said what he said.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 51:

His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿The king said, "What was your business when you sought to seduce Joseph?"﴾ It is narrated that the king sent to the women, among whom was the wife of the Aziz, and he summoned them and said to them this statement. His saying: ﴿What was your business﴾ means: what was your condition (ḥāl)? It was also said: what was your affair (amr)? His saying: ﴿when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself﴾ he addressed them with this statement, and what is meant is the wife of the Aziz specifically. It was also said: the wife of the Aziz sought him for herself, and the rest of the women commanded him to obey her; therefore he said: ﴿when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself﴾. His saying: ﴿They said, "Ḥāshā lillāh" (Far be Allah from it!)﴾, meaning: "God forbid," ﴿We knew of him no evil﴾, meaning: we knew of him no accusation or betrayal. His saying: ﴿The wife of the Aziz said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed he is of the truthful"﴾. In the story: when the women reported Joseph's innocence of what had been attributed to him, they turned on the wife of the Aziz, reproaching her. It is narrated that she feared they would turn on her and testify against her, so she confessed and said: "Now the truth has become evident." Its meaning: the truth became clear. It was also said: its meaning: now the matter has come to light after being concealed. The poet said:

(Lo, let my message reach Khidāsh, that he is a liar whenever the truth becomes evident, a wrongdoer.)

﴿It was I who sought to seduce him from himself﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

His saying: ﴿And indeed he is of the truthful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 52:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That [is so] that he may know﴾. The scholars differed over whose statement this is. The majority hold that it is the statement of Yusuf. Its meaning: "That is so that the Aziz may know {that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers}." Its meaning: He does not make clear and does not guide the plot of the betrayers.

If someone says: How did Yusuf's statement enter in the middle of this speech, when what is mentioned is a conversation that took place between the king and the women?

We say: The interposition of one statement between another is permissible in the language of the Arabs. Allah the Exalted said, in the story of Sulayman, relating from Bilqis: ﴿She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town, they corrupt it and make the honored of its people humiliated. And thus do they do."﴾ The words of Allah the Exalted are an interposition in the middle. Some of them said: In [the verse] there is a transposition of order, meaning: "Return to your Lord and ask Him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands; indeed my Lord is Knowing of their plot. That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers." Then, in meaning, there follows on from this His saying: ﴿What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 53:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And I do not declare myself innocent; indeed, the soul is most commanding of evil﴾ — the verse. It is narrated that Jibril (peace be upon him) said to Yusuf, when he said: "That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence." [He said to him]: "Nor when you desired her." And it is narrated that he said: "When you untied the belt." Then Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not declare myself innocent﴾, ﴿indeed, the soul is most commanding of evil﴾.
