(Men wish that I would die, and if I die, / then that is a way in which I am not unique.)

And His saying: ﴿upon insight﴾, meaning: upon certainty (yaqin). Basirah (basirah, "insight") is the knowledge by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood. And His saying: ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾, its meaning: I call to Allah, and whoever follows me also calls to Allah. Some of them said: the speech is complete at His saying ﴿I call to Allah﴾, then he resumed and said: ﴿upon insight, I and whoever follows me﴾. And His saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah, and I am not of the polytheists﴾, meaning: I say, "Glory be to Allah, and I am not of the polytheists."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 109:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We sent before you only men, to whom We revealed, from among the people of the towns﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah did not send any prophet from among the Bedouins (badw); rather, Allah sent the prophets from among the cities (amsar) and the towns (qura). He also said: Allah did not send any prophet from among the jinn, nor from among women. It was said: Allah did not send any prophet from among the desert dwellers (al-badiyah), because of their harshness and coarseness. As for the people of the cities, they are [more tender] of heart, more intelligent, and more perceptive in matters; therefore Allah sent the prophets from among them. And His words: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

And His words: ﴿And the Hereafter abode is better﴾ — its meaning: "and the state in the Hereafter abode," for a person has two states: the first state (al-hal al-ula) and the final state (al-hal al-akhira). It was also said: "and the abode of the Hereafter" is an idafa (construct) of a thing to itself, like their saying: ﴿better for those who are righteous﴾, "the day of Thursday" and "the day of Friday." The poet said:

(Do you praise Fazʿa and blame ʿAbs? ... Woe to you by Allah, your mother is a hybrid!)

(Had the abode of ʿAbs been victorious over you ... you would have known humiliation with the knowledge of certainty.) He made ʿirfan (recognition) an idafa to yaqin (certainty).

And His words: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ — will you not then understand.

The Exalted said: ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾. It has been recited in two ways, with shadd (tashdid) and with takhfif (lightening). The people of Kufa recited it with takhfif. The verse is problematic when recited with takhfif, because the questioner says: how could the messengers think that they had been lied to? That is not permissible for the prophets. ʿĀʾisha used to reject this recitation and say: it is only "kudhdhibū" with tashdid, meaning that the messengers thought that those who believed in them would deny them, because of the severity of the trial and affliction upon them and the lengthening of the period for them. This was narrated by al-Zuhri from ʿUrwa from ʿĀʾisha. And from Qatada: the ẓann (thought) here has the meaning of yaqīn (certainty), and its meaning is: the messengers were certain that the people had denied them with a denial after which their faith was not hoped for. This is an emphasis of His saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾, because its meaning is: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, that is, they despaired. As for the recitation with takhfif, this is a sound recitation, and it is transmitted from ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and many of the Companions.

Regarding its meaning there are two opinions. The first: what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: the hearts of the messengers weakened, though they were human, by the lengthening of time and the abundance of delay. God the Exalted said in another place: ﴿and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God?"﴾ And His saying: ﴿When is the help of God?﴾ is a request for hastening, or they said this out of human weakness.

The second opinion, which is the correct one, and which is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, is that the meaning of the verse is: those who believed in the messengers thought that the messengers had been denied (with takhfif), or the people to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had been denied (with takhfif). Mujahid recited: "wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhdhibū", and its meaning, as we mentioned in the second opinion, is that the people thought that the messengers had been denied.

His saying: ﴿[there came to them] Our help﴾ is clear in meaning. His saying: ﴿and whom We will were delivered﴾: the will (mashīʾa) applies to the believers. His saying: ﴿and Our might is not turned back from the guilty people﴾: i.e., Our punishment (bas), ﴿from the people who are criminals﴾, i.e., from the disbelieving people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 12, verse 111:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson﴾ meaning: an indication and a sign.

His saying: ﴿for people of understanding﴾ meaning: for people of intellects.

And His saying: ﴿it was not a narration that could be invented﴾ meaning: [fabricated], i.e., the story of Yusuf.

And His saying: ﴿but a confirmation of what was before it﴾ meaning: of the Torah and the Gospel.

And His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ meaning: of the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and the prohibitions, the promises and the threats. And His saying: ﴿and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾ (its meaning: a clarification and a blessing for a people who believe). And Allah knows best what is correct.
